summary: The OpPhi loop-carried SSA design is fundamentally SOUND: I verified the real emit_for_range CFG (body.rs 738-814), the existing short-circuit OpPhi usage (1370-1374), the prelude coopmat SSA binding set (446-452), the HirStmt::Assign store path (496-503), the HIR typecheck Assign arms (1019-1066 flat + 1611-1654 nested), and the example kernels. The CFG matches the architect's predecessor model (header reached from pre-header + continue/latch back-edge), rspirv 0.12 supports Mechanism 1 cleanly (module_mut + select_block + insert_into_block(InsertPoint::Begin)), the OQ-A scalar-vs-OpPhi split is TRUE, and the TFLOPS methodology is honest. NEEDS_REVISION (not REJECT) for ONE under-specified hard requirement that the design hedges as 'possibly/if not present' when it is in fact DEFINITELY REQUIRED: the typecheck Assign path currently CANNOT typecheck `acc = coopmat_mul_add(...)` (it routes the RHS through check_expr with expected_ty=None, which triggers CoopMatrixBuiltinRequiresExpectedType). Plus several CFG/exit-state correctness clarifications the Coder must not get wrong.
critical_issues: CRITICAL (must fix in spec, currently HEDGED as 'possibly'): Pattern B (`acc = coopmat_mul_add(a,b,acc)`) does NOT typecheck today. BOTH Assign arms — flat typecheck.rs:1052-1055 and NESTED typecheck.rs:1641-1643 — compute `scalar_expected = binding_ty.as_scalar()` which is None for a CoopMatrix binding, then call check_expr(..., None). A coopmat builtin call with no expected matrix-type context raises TypecheckError::CoopMatrixBuiltinRequiresExpectedType (typecheck.rs:386-387). The matmul reassign lives INSIDE the K-loop, so it is the NESTED arm (1611-1654) that must be fixed: route coopmat-target Assign through check_coopmat_init_expr(&tc, value, span, matrix_key) exactly like the Let arm (1002-1005), AND validate the RHS coopmat use_==Accumulator matches the target. The architect's §A.6 calls this 'possibly NO change' / 'if not present' — that is WRONG; it is a guaranteed hard error today and a MANDATORY change. Demote the hedge to a firm requirement and name BOTH arms.

CRITICAL (verify, do not silently miscompile): HirStmt::Assign in body.rs:496-503 does unconditional b.store(var_id, val_id). For a coopmat binding, var_ids[binding] holds the SSA RESULT id (a matrix value), NOT an OpVariable pointer — b.store to a non-pointer is invalid SPIR-V and rspirv may or may not catch it. The architect's fix (branch on coopmat_binding_ids → var_ids.insert SSA-rebind, no store) is correct and MUST land together with PART A; an AT-1701-style spirv-val gate must run before any kernel rewrite.

CRITICAL (exit-state for nested loops + post-loop read): The design says 'on emit_for_range exit set var_ids[B]=phi_id'. This is correct for a post-loop store and for zero-trip. But verify it composes for NESTED loops: when the INNER loop returns and sets var_ids[B]=inner_phi_id, the OUTER loop's latch-value capture (step A.4.5) must read the value PRODUCED BY the inner loop's merge, i.e. inner_phi_id — which is exactly what the inner loop left in var_ids[B]. For the matmul the acc update is single-level (outer K-loop only), so this is moot in the shipped fixture, but AT-1702 (two coopmat phis + inner loop) exercises it. Demand the test assert the OUTER phi's latch operand == the inner loop's merged value id, not a stale pre-inner id.

CRITICAL (selected-block restoration): Mechanism 1 does select_block(header_idx) + insert_into_block(Begin, phi) AFTER the merge block has been opened. The Builder's selected_block is then the header, not the merge. emit_for_range MUST select_block back to the merge block (or perform the dr-insert BEFORE opening merge) so subsequent emission lands in the right block. The design does not state this; a missing re-selection corrupts all post-loop emission. Make it explicit.
warnings: WARNING: detect_loop_carried_coopmat condition (b) requires B 'already present in var_ids with a defined SSA id at loop entry'. A coopmat binding that is let-initialized BEFORE the loop is in var_ids (Let handler inserts the init SSA id, body.rs:484). But the detection runs at emit_for_range START — confirm the Vec ordering is deterministic (the design cites AT-326 declaration order; enforce by iterating body.bindings order, not HashSet iteration, to avoid non-deterministic phi emission order across multiple carried values).

WARNING: InsertPoint::Begin inserts at block.instructions[0]; block.instructions does NOT include the OpLabel (separate block.label field in rspirv dr), so index 0 is genuinely the first non-label instruction — correct. But multiple phis must be inserted in REVERSE source order so they end at indices 0..k in declaration order (architect noted this; QA must assert order in AT-1702).

WARNING: break-to-merge reasoning is subtle but correct: a break edge targets merge, NOT header, so it does NOT add a header-phi predecessor — the phi predecessor set stays exactly {pre_header, latch}. However, if a coopmat accumulator is consumed AFTER the loop and a break occurred, the merge sees the phi value of the breaking trip (the value at the START of that trip, pre-reassignment). For a matmul that is acceptable (no break), but the conservative continue-rejection (AT-1704) does NOT cover break-skipping-reassignment. Confirm matmul/attention have no break over a carried coopmat; if a future kernel does, document the semantics.

WARNING (honesty / title): the milestone is titled 'competitive matmul' but a single-16x16-coopmat-tile-per-workgroup shared-staged kernel will very likely land at a modest % of the 125-TFLOPS cuBLAS datasheet estimate (cuBLAS uses register blocking, multi-warp tiles, double buffering — none present here). The design IS honest in prose ('report whatever it is'), but DESIGN.md §3.1.15 must NOT be filled in with the word 'competitive' unless the measured number warrants it. The honest deliverable is effective-TFLOPS + bit-exactness from one annotated source, not a competitiveness claim.
spirv_concerns: SPIR-V 2.4 'All OpPhi instructions must be the first instructions in a block': satisfied by InsertPoint::Begin (lands before the induction OpLoad). VERIFIED feasible in rspirv 0.12 (module_mut/select_block/insert_into_block all public, dr/build/mod.rs:126-150,314).

SPIR-V §2.16 OpPhi predecessor completeness: the header's CFG predecessors are EXACTLY {pre-header (initial OpBranch at body.rs:753), continue/latch (back-edge OpBranch at body.rs:805)}. body and merge are NOT header predecessors. The two-operand phi {(pre_header_value, pre_header_label), (latch_value, continue_label)} matches precisely. CONFIRMED against the real CFG. spirv-val Vulkan_1_1 will reject any deviation — AT-1701's predecessor-walk + spirv-val is the correct double gate.

Header predecessor caveat the Coder MUST honor: pre_header_label must be captured via current_block_label() BEFORE the OpBranch to header (body.rs:753), i.e. the block we branch FROM — which may NOT be the kernel entry block if the loop is preceded by an if/another loop's merge. The design says 'capture before OpStore i_var start / OpBranch header' — correct, but emphasize it is the dynamically-current block, not a fixed entry label.

GLSL.std.450 Exp2 (PART C, OQ-C): co-exists with the f32 attention's plain GLSL450 memory model (attention is NOT coopmat). No conflict. If exp2 is added, the ext-inst-set import id must be created once and threaded; the additive KernelResources.ext_glsl_std_450: Option<Word> field is sound.
vendor_concerns: Lavapipe has no CooperativeMatrixKHR: AT-1620/1622/1710 MUST typed-skip on CoopMatUnsupported (design states this). AT-1621 (f32) + AT-1630 (f32 attention) run on Lavapipe — these are the only CI-executable correctness gates for M3.3, so the f32 matmul index-math fix and attention dispatch-geometry fix carry the real-GPU anti-pattern-#9 burden on CI; the coopmat OpPhi correctness is only proven on self-hosted NVIDIA. Acceptable but note CI cannot prove the coopmat phi numerics — only spirv-val + structural dr-walk on CI.
missing_tests: MUST TEST: a NEGATIVE typecheck test that `acc = coopmat_mul_add(...)` on a `let mut acc: matrix[...,accumulator]` NOW typechecks (currently fails with CoopMatrixBuiltinRequiresExpectedType) — guards the CRITICAL-1 fix. Without it, regression is silent.

MUST TEST: a typecheck test that reassigning a NON-accumulator coopmat (use_ A or B) is rejected (CoopMatReassignNonAccumulator or shape mismatch) — the Assign path must validate use_==Accumulator, not just element type.
MUST TEST (AT-1702): assert the OUTER loop phi's latch operand id == the value the INNER loop left in var_ids (nested composition), not merely 'two phis exist'.
MUST TEST: spirv-val on the f32 matmul AND attention AFTER the index/dispatch fixes (anti-pattern #9 on Lavapipe), with max_diff vs CPU reference — these are the CI-runnable correctness proofs.
MUST TEST (AT-1703): the post-loop coopmat_store source operand id == the header phi id (proves var_ids[B]=phi_id on exit), AND a zero-trip dynamic dispatch yields coopmat_zero output bit-exactly.
questions_for_architect: OQ-B firm answer required: does lower.rs allocate a fresh BindingId for a re-`let` with the same name? If yes (likely), Pattern A is forbidden for coopmat and Pattern B (let mut + Assign) is the ONLY supported form — and then BOTH the nested-Assign typecheck routing (CRITICAL-1) and the body.rs Assign SSA-rebind (CRITICAL-2) are MANDATORY, not optional. Confirm the lowering empirically as the FIRST coder step.

OQ-D: pin Mechanism 1 (insert_into_block(InsertPoint::Begin)) — it is fully supported in rspirv 0.12 (verified). Drop Mechanism 2 (OpCopyObject placeholder) unless Mechanism 1 fails spirv-val, to avoid two code paths. State the selected-block-restoration step explicitly.
Will DESIGN.md §3.1.15 / ROADMAP refrain from the word 'competitive' if the measured TFLOPS is low-single-digit %? Commit to reporting the bare number + bit-exactness as the deliverable.
oq_a_split_confirmation: CONFIRMED TRUE. matmul_shared_f32.axc uses `let mut acc: f32` (line 47) updated by `acc = acc + a_val*b_val` (line 73) — a SCALAR on the Function-storage path that already works (reduction.axc). Its gpu=0.0 is a pure index bug: tile_row=gid(1) (line 40) AND local_row=gid(1) (line 43) are IDENTICAL, so out_row=tile_row*16+local_row=gid(1)*16+gid(1) scatters writes to wrong indices, leaving most of C zero. NO OpPhi needed. tiled_attention.axc uses `let mut max_score/denom/out_val: f32` (lines 62,92,121) — all SCALAR, Function-storage, already working; gpu=0.0 is @workgroup(1,1,1) + q_row=gid(0) requiring a (seq_len,1,1) dispatch (host geometry bug). NO OpPhi needed. PART A (OpPhi) is required ONLY for matmul_shared_coopmat.axc's coopmat accumulator. The split is correctly attributed; the only OpPhi-dependent kernel is the coopmat matmul.
oq_e_position: ACCEPT the methodology, DEMAND title-honesty. The resident bench infra (CUBLAS_F32_GEMM_TFLOPS_RTX_PRO_6000=125 datasheet const, effective_tflops, MIN-of-N, GpuTimestamp, 50GB cap, typed-skip) already exists in resident_matmul.rs and is honest — % of a LABELED datasheet estimate, never asserted against a ratio. A same-machine cuBLAS A/B is out of thesis scope (CUDA-free) and correctly NOT required. The realistic number for one 16x16 coopmat tile/workgroup is modest; the design must report it as-is and NOT write 'competitive' into DESIGN.md/ROADMAP unless the measured value justifies it. Effective-TFLOPS + bit-exactness from a single annotated source is the real deliverable.
most_dangerous_hole: The typecheck gap (CRITICAL-1): Pattern B `acc = coopmat_mul_add(...)` does NOT compile today and the design HEDGES this as 'possibly NO change' / 'if not present'. If the Coder takes the hedge at face value, they will implement PART A's body.rs SSA-rebind, write the multi-K-block kernel, and hit a HARD typecheck error (CoopMatrixBuiltinRequiresExpectedType) on the NESTED Assign arm — discovering only mid-implementation that the typecheck Assign path must be rewritten to route coopmat targets through check_coopmat_init_expr with the binding's CoopMatKey AND validate use_==Accumulator. This is the single most likely place to either stall the milestone or (worse) hack around it by reverting to Pattern A re-let, which then breaks BindingId stability and silently produces a phi reading the wrong predecessor value = malformed SPIR-V or zero output. Pin Pattern B, pin the nested-Assign coopmat typecheck routing as MANDATORY, and gate it with a positive + negative typecheck test before any kernel rewrite.
summary_verdict: NEEDS_REVISION: the OpPhi CFG/predecessor/ordering/dominance design is provably correct against the real emit_for_range CFG and rspirv 0.12 (Mechanism 1 fully supported); the OQ-A scalar-vs-OpPhi split is TRUE; OQ-E is honest. Revise to: (1) demote the typecheck Assign-coopmat change from 'possibly' to MANDATORY, naming the NESTED arm (typecheck.rs:1611-1654) and the check_coopmat_init_expr routing + use_==Accumulator validation, with positive+negative typecheck tests; (2) state the selected-block restoration step after the dr-insert; (3) require AT-1702 to assert nested phi latch-operand composition; (4) bind DESIGN.md/ROADMAP to report the bare TFLOPS number without the word 'competitive' unless measured. With those four revisions the design is APPROVE-ready.
